problems.stem: A draft screen asks novices to read a dense paragraph while a narrator reads different text aloud. In a cognitive load diagnosis, this is best classified as which kind of load, and why?
options: Intrinsic load, because the content is inherently hard.
Extraneous load, because the redundant on-screen text and mismatched narration force the learner to reconcile two sources, which the design could remove.
Germane load, because the learner is building a schema.
No load, because narration always helps.
problems.explanation: Redundant or conflicting text and audio is a classic extraneous-load source introduced by the design. It is removable, unlike intrinsic load from the content itself.

problems.stem: A teammate proposes "reducing cognitive load" by deleting the practice problems from a lesson. Why is this the wrong move in a load diagnosis?
options: Practice generates germane load, the productive effort of building schemas; cutting it lowers total effort but also removes the learning, so it is not the load you want to reduce.
Deleting practice always raises extraneous load.
Practice problems are intrinsic load and cannot be changed.
problems.explanation: Not all load is bad. Germane load is the useful effort of learning. A diagnosis should cut extraneous load, not the germane load that drives schema construction.

problems.stem: You ask an AI tool to label each screen of your draft as high, medium, or low cognitive load. It returns confident ratings with no source attribution. What is the strongest bounded use?
options: Adopt the AI ratings as your diagnosis because they are consistent.
Treat the ratings as prompts to inspect, then assign each load to a type (intrinsic, extraneous, germane) with the specific screen evidence that justifies it.
Ask the AI to also redesign every high-load screen automatically.
Average the AI ratings into a single module-level score and report that.
problems.explanation: A load diagnosis must name the type of load and point to the screen feature causing it. An undifferentiated high or low rating from AI is not a diagnosis the designer can act on.

problems.stem: Your draft introduces a complex statistics topic to true beginners and the intrinsic load is high. Which revision most defensibly manages that load without removing the content?
options: Delete the hardest example so the topic feels easier.
Use segmenting and worked-example pre-training so the high element interactivity is encountered in smaller, sequenced chunks rather than all at once.
Speed up the narration so learners spend less time on it.
Add more decorative visuals to make the topic engaging.
problems.explanation: Intrinsic load from high element interactivity is managed by sequencing and pre-training, not by deletion or decoration. The content stays; the demand is staged.
